user_intent: User asks for a serial dilution protocol on a Hamilton STAR liquid handler; they likely want runnable method code.

tools.name: PyLabRobot (Chatterbox backend + Visualizer)
tools.notes: Use the STARChatterboxBackend to exercise Hamilton STAR API calls without a robot; Visualizer provides a browser-based deck/state view. Good for catching API misuse and basic deck/volume constraints before touching hardware. Docs emphasize PLR is distinct from PyHamilton and runs cross‑platform. ([docs.pylabrobot.org](https://docs.pylabrobot.org/user_guide/00_liquid-handling/hamilton-star/hamilton-liquid-classes.html?utm_source=openai))

tools.name: PyHamilton (simulate mode)
tools.notes:
Community Python interface for STAR/STARlet. Can run on a PC not connected to a robot using from pyhamilton import HamiltonInterface
with HamiltonInterface(simulate=True) as ham:
    pass  # dry-run context opens without hardware to validate imports and API calls; requires Hamilton VENUS installed on Windows. ([github.com](https://github.com/dgretton/pyhamilton))

tools.name: Hamilton VENUS Run Control (Simulation Mode)
tools.notes: Official offline simulation in VENUS; training indicates no liquid handler required to develop/run during course access. Simulation mode is controlled in VENUS/Run Control (can be toggled via settings/config, not at runtime by API). ([hamiltoncompany.com](https://www.hamiltoncompany.com/automated-liquid-handling/training/vb_r_pac25.10?utm_source=openai))
tools.usage_example: N/A (open Run Control, load method, run in Simulation Mode)

tools.name: Hamilton HSL Method Editor (HxHSLMetEd)
tools.notes: Used to author and validate HSL; supports file/library validation and catches HSL syntax issues referenced in VENUS documentation and community guidance. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/991990355/VENUS-21-CFR-Part-11-Guide-Rev-B?utm_source=openai))

simulation_validation_via_code.notes: Python-based approaches (PyLabRobot, PyHamilton) enable script-level checks without hardware: run PLR Chatterbox + Visualizer for API/deck/volume constraints; PyHamilton simulate=True for VENUS-backed dry-runs on a Windows PC. For native VENUS/HSL methods, use HSL Method Editor for syntax and Run Control Simulation Mode for offline execution. VENUS also provides built-in Serial Dilution via Power Steps if staying in the GUI. ([docs.pylabrobot.org](https://docs.pylabrobot.org/user_guide/00_liquid-handling/hamilton-star/hamilton-liquid-classes.html?utm_source=openai))

recommendation: To develop a serial dilution method without hardware, prefer PyLabRobot with the STARChatterboxBackend and Visualizer to iterate and catch API/constraint issues, then move to firmware/robot when ready. —no robot needed. ([docs.pylabrobot.org](https://docs.pylabrobot.org/user_guide/00_liquid-handling/hamilton-star/hamilton-liquid-classes.html?utm_source=openai))
